newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait will not borrow to cover budget deficit.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait will not borrow to cover budget deficit.

text.p: Kuwait, which has vowed never to borrow again from world markets, will cover a 1997/98 gross budget deficit projected on Tuesday at 1.584 billion dinars ($5.204 billion) from general reserves.
"If there will be a deficit, it will be covered from the reserves. They have the money," a leading economist said about the 4.378-billion dinar budget passed by parliament on Tuesday.
Parliament approved the budget statement saying the deficit "will be covered from reserve funds of the state."

Economists said Kuwait could report a slight surplus in the 4.21 billion dinar 1996/97 budget for the fiscal year ended on June 30 due to a sharp rise in world oil prices. That surplus forecast compares with a projected 1.51 billion dinar gross deficit.
Oil revenue is calculated at a conservative estimate of $13 a barrel. Kuwait, which controls 10 percent of the world's oil reserves, has an OPEC daily quota of two million barrels.
In December, the oil-rich Gulf Arab state completed on schedule repayment of a $5.5 billion sovereign loan and outstanding principle to wipe out all long-term foreign debts.

The jumbo loan was taken after the 1991 Gulf War to free Kuwait from a seven-month Iraqi occupation to pay mainly for huge reconstruction costs while work was underway to restore oil export capabilities.
Some 80 banks from 19 countries extended the J.P. Morgan and Co arranged loan, which at the time, was the largest ever made to a sovereign state.
Central Bank Governor Sheikh Salem Abdul-Aziz al- Sabah has said Kuwait would not borrow from international markets again.
Officials told Reuters in April Kuwait would complete payment of $600 million in export finance over the next couple of years, clearing all foreign debts.
